Twenty-one comments

Composer

Several pages on the web credit Joan MacDonald Boes as the composer. BTW, I was glad to find this tune, I was particularly looking for it. I believe it’s also on Lisa Carthy’s album Red Rice.

↳ Posted by ThosG on August 1st, 2003.

Isn’t it a Jerry Holland tune? Eliza Carthy recorded it as a traditional tune, though.

↳ Posted by slainte on August 1st, 2003.

yes, jerry holland plays it. but if you check the notes for his ‘master cape breton fiddler’ album, he attributes it to joan macdonald boes.

sarah in portland

↳ Posted by Sarah Cardin on November 25th, 2003.

Alternate Version

This also gets played with the last four bars of the A part being substituted for the last four bars of the B part the second time through. Kind of a nice way to bring it to an ending. This is in one of my scottish tunebooks in A, but G is a bit easier for many instruments.

↳ Posted by AlBrown on October 7th, 2004.

This is pretty close to the way Alasdair Fraser plays it -- the Saltfishforty version is played with much more of a slow Shetland swing, with dotted crotchet pairs instead of some of the triplets.

All that said, what a lovely tune!

G or A?

I’ve played it through roughly in G and then A; it really sounds great in both, and I may practise it playing twice through in G then once through in A. I play two or three tunes this way, changing key on the same tune; as an example, Bill Harty’s Jig, going from D to A. (a simple change for fiddle/banjo/mandolin, just going across one string higher.)

The Sweetness Of Mary, X:9

As played, in F major, by Calum Stewart (Track 3 Calum Stewart & Heikki Bourgault, self-released CD 2010).
(I have added transpositions of his setting in G and A within the one ABC addition.)

As Calum & Heikki’s eponymous 2010 album is currently unavailable in hard copy or anywhere online to stream, you can (for the time being) listen to/download the track featuring this tune here: https://app.box.com/s/9ngvjr79lat87ikem1zc9mgfhd5s3qzu

As often in traditional music, transcribing the actual timing of the figures on the 2nd and 4th beats of bars A1, A5 and B 2nd time 5 accurately isn’t really possible – I chose quaver plus 2 semiquavers, others choose a triplet of quavers: neither choice is quite right as those groups of three notes are actually played somewhere between the two choices, with the 1st note of each group of 3 slightly emphasised and long and the 2nd and 3rd notes shorter, without the even emphasis of a true triplet, yet not quite as clipped as in an accurately timed quaver plus 2 semiquavers. For that matter, the dotted quaver-semiquaver pairs and the scotch snaps – semiquaver-dotted quaver – wouldn’t be played absolutely strictly 3:1 (1:3), nor yet are they in triplet time played 2:1 (1:2), but again, somewhere between those timings.

You can also download my transcription document (staff and ABC notations) from: https://app.box.com/s/nsw33hbdht1pwcxq1h83wlogq2t5z0jn

↳ Posted by Jemtheflute on April 26th, 2021.
